title: Buyers vs Sellers
hook: Price isn't moving because your candle turned green. The candle turned green because price moved.

launchpad.outcome: Explain what buyer and seller aggression means — without treating any single candle as the whole story.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does one red candle after a string of green candles automatically mean sellers are in control?

markers.label: Why one candle isn't the whole story

blocks.heading: What buyers and sellers actually do

beats.heading: Buyers showing aggression
beats.body: Participants willing to transact at increasingly higher available prices — that's what pushes price up.

beats.heading: Sellers showing aggression
beats.body: Participants willing to transact at increasingly lower available prices — that's what pushes price down.

beats.heading: One candle isn't the whole story
beats.body: One green candle does NOT establish a bullish market. One red candle does NOT establish a bearish market. This prepares you for reading structure later.

blocks.heading: Is she right?
blocks.scenario: Price prints a small green candle, then a large green candle, then a small red candle. A trader says the red candle means sellers now control the entire market.

options.label: No — one candle without context doesn't tell us the larger structural story
options.feedback: Right. We need more than one candle to know whether the bigger story actually changed.

options.label: Yes — any red candle after green ones means sellers have taken over
options.feedback: One candle isn't enough evidence to declare a full change of control.

blocks.quote: Stop asking what one candle means by itself. Eventually, we'll learn to ask what that candle is doing within structure.

seeIt.heading: Watch control shift on a real path
seeIt.prompt: This path steps higher with a couple of small pullbacks, then something changes.

stages.caption: This price path has been stepping higher, with a couple of small pullbacks along the way.

highlight.label: Still an uptrend — just a shallow pullback

stages.caption: Buyers are still winning here. A small pullback inside an uptrend isn't a change of control.
Same story — buyers are still in control through this point.

highlight.label: This is where it actually broke

stages.caption: Here's where price actually closed lower and broke the pattern — a real shift, not just a wick.

tryIt.heading: Find the shift
tryIt.prompt: Same skill, new chart each time. Tap the point where control actually changed.

rounds.prompt: This path steps higher with a couple of small pullbacks. Tap the point where sellers actually took control.

points.label: Point A
points.feedback: That's a small pullback inside an uptrend that's still holding — not a real change of control.

points.label: Point B
points.feedback: Exactly. That's the point where price actually closed lower and broke the pattern — a real shift, not just a wick.

points.label: Point C
points.feedback: Another shallow pullback — buyers were still winning through this point.

rounds.prompt: Different chart, same question. This path steps lower with a couple of small bounces. Tap the point where buyers actually took control.

points.label: Point A
points.feedback: That's a small bounce inside a downtrend that's still holding — not a real change of control.

points.label: Point B
points.feedback: Exactly — that's where price broke the pattern of lower lows and actually turned. A real shift, not just a bounce.

points.label: Point C
points.feedback: Another shallow bounce — sellers were still winning through this point.

sayItBack.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "How do you know when buyers actually lost control, and not just a normal pullback?" How would you explain it to her?
sayItBack.modelAnswer: A normal pullback still respects the overall pattern — price dips a little but keeps making higher highs and higher lows overall. A real shift is when price actually breaks that pattern — closes lower than the recent structure was allowing, not just wicks into it. One candle never tells you that on its own; you need to see the pattern actually break, not just wiggle.

checklist: Buyer aggression pushes price up; seller aggression pushes price down.
One candle doesn't establish a trend or a reversal on its own.
A real shift breaks the pattern — a normal pullback doesn't.
Later, you'll learn to read what a candle is doing within structure — not just by itself.

takeaways: Buyer aggression pushes price up; seller aggression pushes price down.

remember: Don't ask what one candle means by itself.
